races.name: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground with Harry Skelton in the saddle, and Dan Skelton's stable in strong recent form (7/26 T14); a genuine front-runner who finds himself in a perfect scenario with no pace pressure — the STYLE_FIT tag is a marginal concern given only one rival is likely to genuinely contest the lead.

runners_data.name: Master Haku
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's prominent racer has a win and two places from five Good-ground starts and steps up marginally in trip; Sean Bowen knows how to position a horse from the front rank, and the class ceiling here (OR 119) makes him the most dangerous rival to the leader turning in.

runners_data.name: Nobotheratall
runners_data.note: Smart enough form to win on Good ground twice recently, but this horse's natural desire to race up with the pace is compromised here — with Loriko and Master Haku likely to fill the prominent slots, he may find himself racing in a position that doesn't suit, which genuinely tempers his prospects regardless of raw ability.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with consistent placing form and tongue tie, but OR 69 represents the lowest-rated runner in the field by some margin; he wants to race prominently yet the busier end of the field is already taken, so he may find himself in a midfield role that blunts whatever chance he carries at this class level.

runners_data.name: Arcimboldo
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up horse from Mike Sowersby's small yard, carrying a 3lb claim for Charlie Maggs; has yet to win or place in five hurdles starts and all previous form came on Standard artificial surfaces — the step to Good turf over 2m4½f represents an unknown quantity, and a bigger confidence run is a more realistic outcome than a win.

runners_data.name: Show Your Hand
runners_data.note: Tongue tie applied, just 17 days since last run, and two second-place finishes on Good ground suggest he handles conditions; a true hold-up type who needs a genuinely run race — his best chance is if the pace boils over, but in a six-runner field with a single front-runner, he may simply get too little to aim at coming off the home bend.

races.paceDynamic: Loriko is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field, is set to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo on Good ground over 2m4½f at Market Rasen. Master Haku is the main prominent threat from stall, but with Nobotheratall and Ballinoulart both natural front-runners who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, the field holds more pace-hungry types than the race shape can accommodate — Loriko and Master Haku are most likely to actually secure prominent berths, with Nobotheratall the next most likely to press forward if the pace is judged insufficient. The two hold-up horses, Arcimboldo and Show Your Hand, will need a truly run race to be delivered late, but a lone, uncontested front-runner creating a muddling pace is the least likely scenario to generate the gaps they need. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles — horses close to or on the pace who can maintain rhythm and pounce turning for home, with Loriko and Master Haku best positioned to exploit the race as it is most likely to unfold.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loriko Controls, Wins Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko leads uncontested and sets a sustainable rhythm that the field cannot disrupt.
scenarios.body: Loriko bowls along in front at a metronomic Good-ground gallop, drawing the sting from any challengers by the home turn and kicking clear from the last; Harry Skelton's positioning on a horse with back-to-back wins and strong Good-ground form makes this the standout likely shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Master Haku Presses and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Master Haku tracks Loriko closely throughout and asserts his class from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen positions Master Haku right on Loriko's quarters, and Gordon Elliott's horse — with a win and multiple places at this level on similar ground — produces a smoother jump at the last to go past; the higher OR class of 119 and strong 2m+ hurdles form give him the profile to reverse form if Loriko has done fractionally too much work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Crumbles, Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other out and the hold-up pair get a clear run late.
scenarios.body: Arcimboldo or Show Your Hand, if delivered with a well-timed late sweep, could grab a place from a tired leader, but both are genuine hold-up types dependent on a faster-than-expected pace — Show Your Hand has placed twice from hold-up on Good, and Arcimboldo has yet to win; their chance is real only if the race becomes a proper test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early Pace Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If Nobotheratall forces his way forward and forces a pace duel with Loriko that unravels the race.
scenarios.body: Nobotheratall, a genuine prominent type crowded out of position, could push up alongside Loriko and create a genuine war of attrition in the middle mile, scrambling the race shape entirely; this opens the door for any horse, but it remains a low-probability scenario given Loriko's Harry Skelton partnership and the small field.

watchPoints.text: Loriko — watch whether Harry Skelton is allowed to stride on and build a lead of two or more lengths by the end of the back straight; if he has clear daylight by then, the race may already be won.

Nobotheratall — watch the early stages for Harry Reed attempting to push forward against Loriko and Master Haku; if he does force a pace duel, the entire race shape shifts and hold-up horses become live players.

Master Haku — watch his jumping, particularly at the fourth and fifth hurdles; Gordon Elliott's horse has a pull in the weights and the class, but a clumsy jump mid-race could cost him the prominent position he needs to win.

Show Your Hand — watch whether Freddie Keighley (5lb claim) can get him into a rhythm early despite the hold-up style; at odds, he represents the best-value late-race interest only if the pace is genuinely strong.

Arcimboldo — watch for any signs of market support given the stable's low strike rate (1/2 T14); the switch from artificial to Good turf is a significant unknown and first-time form on the surface is worth monitoring in running.

races.name: Betway Summer Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Indemnity
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form (2341) and excellent good-going record (8/15 sim-going); Emma Lavelle yard quiet at 0/3 over 14 days, and a 70-day absence is worth noting, but if match-fit this is a competitive profile for the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Indemnity was unplaced last time out but that run came 70 days ago, and the form before it reads a win and two places from his last four. He has run over today's trip and going before and rates second of thirteen here, with such a lengthy absence the main query.

runners_data.name: Moon Chime
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner here; wins at Stratford and good ground suggest competence, but the style-fit flag (0.91) signals this horse is arguably racing out of its most comfortable role given the pressure it may face from a prominent cluster — handicap mark of OR 133 makes it a stiff ask if headed.
runners_data.comment: Moon Chime won last time out and tops our figures here, with two below-par ninths sandwiched between that success and another win four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, back from a 52-day break, with those blank efforts a reminder he can go missing too.

runners_data.name: Howth
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four wins and excellent good-ground course form (3114 recent, all on good); Tom Lacey in decent 14-day form (1/5), and the tight hurdle track at Market Rasen should suit a horse that jumps fluently and travels prominently throughout.
runners_data.comment: Howth was third last time out, continuing a solid campaign that included back-to-back wins three and four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and sits seventh of thirteen on our figures, a fair reflection of a fairly consistent record.

runners_data.name: Louis Veron
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes over on this lightly-raced five-year-old who has won two of his last three starts, all on good ground; Dan Skelton yard firing (7/26 14-day) and the horse's prominent, progressive profile makes him a key player if he gets into his natural position near the front.
runners_data.comment: Louis Veron won his last two starts after finishing runner-up in the two before, a progressive shape to the form, and his trainer is among the in-form yards at 27% over the last fortnight. He has run over today's trip and going before but rates only sixth of thirteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Five wins from his last six completed starts including three in a row, and his good-ground record (9/15) is excellent; Oakley Brown (5) claims five pounds which partially offsets the rise, and the tp headgear combination with that recent form makes him one of the most dangerous prominent types in the race.
runners_data.comment: Newtown Rambler is in red-hot form, winning three in a row and four of his last five, the exception a pulled-up run four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a quick 20-day turnaround, with that one blank the only query.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: In-form horse naturally wanting to race prominently — five consecutive placed efforts on good ground — but with so many similar types in the field, Martin Keighley's runner is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which the style-fit flag (0.91) reflects; watch whether Freddie Keighley (5) can manoeuvre him forward early.
runners_data.comment: Continuance is winless in his last five starts but has been consistently competitive, runner-up last time out and two starts back, with a third and fourth among his other recent starts. He has run over today's trip and going before, quick to reappear on a 15-day break, and rates fifth of thirteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Charlus
runners_data.note: Bleak recent form (FP0P-5) and a hold-up style that relies on others doing the donkey work; the ht headgear combination and soft-going preference (only 1 place from 5 good-ground runs) make this a tough ask in the current conditions, though Dan Skelton's operation always merits respect.
runners_data.comment: Charlus's yard is among the in-form operations right now, striking at 27% over the last fortnight, and he returns quickly on a 15-day break having already run over today's trip and going. The formline is modest — fifth last time out with three non-completions in his last five — but stable form and our rating of 128 keep him interesting.

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race up with the pace but the redistribution reflects the crowded prominent group — Nick Scholfield's charge (STYLE_FIT 0.93) may find himself racing in unfamiliar territory mid-division; the p headgear and two recent wins (including on good ground) suggest ability, but a position too far back would blunt his chance.
runners_data.comment: Morning Mayhem was only fourth last time out and finds this a stiff task at tenth of thirteen on our figures, despite winning two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and the pattern of alternating placed efforts with a couple of wins shows genuine ability, but consistency is clearly the issue.

runners_data.name: Pigeon House
runners_data.note: One of only two genuine hold-up types in the race; recent form includes a win and a placed effort on good ground (521-P2) and the seven-furlong build-up suits this distance, but Charles & Adam Pogson yard quiet at 0/3 over 14 days — needs things to go wrong up front to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Pigeon House was runner-up last time out and has been frequently competitive, with a win three starts back and another second four back, though a pulled-up effort in between is a blot on the record. He has run over today's trip and going before and sits mid-field at eighth of thirteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Squeezebox
runners_data.note: Three wins from four on good ground at this trip and genuinely effective when able to race prominently; Tom Lacey also saddles Howth, splitting stable representation, and the ht headgear flags consistency — the STYLE_FIT concern (0.93) applies only to the extent he cannot get his favoured position, which is a real risk in this field.
runners_data.comment: Squeezebox arrives in good heart, winning his last two starts and three of his last four overall, the exception a fifth three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before but returns from a 46-day break, and rates only ninth of thirteen on our figures despite the strong recent form.

runners_data.name: Letterston Lily
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on good ground last time after an absence and has strong stamina credentials, but 86 days off and a long trip (OR 118) from Wales for Mickey Bowen's yard (0/8, 14 days) creates some caution; naturally prominent but mapped back given the congestion — James Bowen takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Letterston Lily won last time out but that was 86 days ago, and the form before it reads unplaced, fourth and unseated, patchy at best. She has run over today's trip and going before, but such a long absence and eleventh of thirteen on our figures make her hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Mojito Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old with a placid profile (2442) — no wins from four runs, all on good or soft — and the longest absence in the field at 111 days; Harry Cobden adds class in the saddle, and the t headgear is retained, but the horse needs to find improvement on OR 118 to feature.
runners_data.comment: Mojito Des Mottes is winless in his last four starts, alternating seconds and fourths, and hasn't run for 111 days, a big query on fitness alone. He has run over today's trip and going before but rates bottom of thirteen on our figures, making him a tough sell in this company.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Ran just eight days ago (OR 112, lowest in field) and Sean Bowen takes over for James Owen's yard which is active (8/48 14-day); a v headgear switch is notable, and while the horse has won on good ground at 2m, the prominent style mapped back means he needs a significant upgrade at the weights to threaten here.
runners_data.comment: High Fibre was fifth last time out and again two starts back, though the form includes a second three back and a win four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and is race-fit on a quick 8-day turnaround, but rates only twelfth of thirteen on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Moon Chime is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should set a measured, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground over 2m½f at Market Rasen. Indemnity, Howth, Louis Veron, and Newtown Rambler are all prominent-style horses who will want to be close to the pace, creating a competitive early order behind Moon Chime but without the overcrowding at the very front that would produce a true scorching tempo. The field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Continuance, Morning Mayhem, Squeezebox, Letterston Lily, Mojito Des Mottes, and High Fibre are all natural prominent racers who have been mapped to midfield because they simply cannot all get there, with Newtown Rambler and Louis Veron — the classiest and most recently in form of that group — most likely to actually lock up the first three or four positions behind Moon Chime. A controlled, honest gallop with a well-organised prominent group is the overwhelming shape here, and that configuration strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, jump fluently, and quicken from the front half of the field rather than true hold-up types mounting a late challenge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Chime sets an honest but sustainable pace and the race is decided by those who travel prominently and jump cleanly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Moon Chime dictates at a measured tempo, and the prominent horses who secure their position — most likely Newtown Rambler and Louis Veron — press from the second fence out, hitting the line with stamina and momentum intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moon Chime Kicks, Leads Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Chime's uncontested lead allows it to dictate fully and kick decisively from the final hurdle, stealing a march on the field.
scenarios.body: With no horse ever seriously pressuring, Moon Chime builds an unassailable lead turning for home and the prominent chasers are left chasing shadows; this scenario rewards Moon Chime's front-running ability and the tactical failure of rivals to press sooner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves truly modest and several prominent horses move up en masse to challenge Moon Chime from three out, turning it into a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo compresses the field and multiple prominent runners arrive together at the last, producing a sprint finish where jumping accuracy at the final hurdle is decisive; horses with the highest recent class and sharpest TS figures prosper.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely brisk enough to cause attrition and a true hold-up runner picks up the pieces from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine pace collapse among the prominent group, which is unlikely given Moon Chime's typically measured front-running, but Pigeon House and Charlus are the only genuine hold-up types capable of benefiting.

watchPoints.text: Newtown Rambler's five-from-six winning streak on good ground paired with Oakley Brown's five-pound claim makes him a critical runner to monitor — if he secures a prominent position early, he is the most dangerous horse in the race based on recent form and strike rate.

Louis Veron with Harry Skelton aboard for the in-form Skelton yard (7/26, 14-day) is a potent combination; watch how quickly he is asked to move up from a prominent position, as the horse has won his last two and clearly relishes these conditions.

The redistribution of six prominent-style runners means the early stages could see unexpected shuffling and crowding behind Moon Chime — any horse that gets hampered or loses its position at the first two hurdles may find the race over before it starts.

Charlus carries a stop-start form profile (FP0P-5) and has shown a clear preference for soft ground over good; if the going description holds, watch for an early weakening signal from this hold-up type that could disrupt runners immediately behind it.

Moon Chime's uncontested lead is the structural pivot of the whole race — if it is allowed to bowl along at its own pace unchallenged past halfway, the race shape becomes strongly front-runner-biassed and the chasing pack may need to produce career-best efforts to peg it back.

races.name: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Steeple Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mahons Glory
runners_data.note: Trained by Dylan Cunha and ridden by Lee Edwards, this 10-year-old has won over comparable good-ground trips (1/22f/GOO) and is the only confirmed lead horse here; the slight concern is a 2164 recent form sequence suggesting he can be caught, but as the race-shaper everything flows through him.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has two wins in its last five starts, having run over today's trip and going before and fit again after a 29-day break. A below-form sixth three starts back is the only blemish on a progressive profile.

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride on this Keiran Burke-trained nine-year-old who has been off 99 days — the lengthy layoff is notable and his recent form reads U45B-, but on good ground at this trip he has placed; naturally prominent, he is well-placed to fill the slot immediately behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Unseated four starts back and brought down last time out, leaving it yet to score in its last four starts, but it already has experience over today's trip and going. Tops our figures in this field, so the concern is fitness after 99 days off, not ability.

runners_data.name: Riaan
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends this nine-year-old over from Ireland and T14 figures of 10/59 show the yard is firing; suited by good ground (1/21f/GOO in history) and wears a tongue strap and back bar, but a P014-0 string shows inconsistency and the step up to 2m5½f on a flat-ish track is the question mark.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, with the class to feature having already run over today's trip and going before. Reliability is the query though - unplaced last time out, and pulled up five starts back - meaning things need to go its way for another success.

runners_data.name: Gunsight Ridge
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old for Mike Sowersby who has only 2/15 similar-going runs in his profile — good ground is a concern — and the 4476-3 recent form puts him in the third/fourth category rather than win column; tongue strap worn, 55 days off, but Jonathan Burke is a reliable pilot.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, with 6th, 7th and two 4ths before that, leaving it winless in its last five starts. Already run over today's trip and going and fit again despite a 55-day break, so an improved placing is within reach if the shape of the race suits.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: In-form eight-year-old for Tristan Davidson who arrives on just 20 days' rest; form reads 51-321 and his historical record shows 2W7P on good or equivalent — he is the standout candidate for the prominent second position and has strong claims if the pace is as measured as expected.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has two wins in its last five starts, aided by a runner-up and third in that spell. Already run over today's trip and going and fresh again after 20 days, but ranks only seventh of 13 here, leaving more to find against the front-runners.

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners this Mickey Bowen-trained mare (0/8 yard in 14 days), who has been running consistently without winning (P50-33 recent); wears a tongue strap and has seven placings from 14 good-ground runs, making her a place candidate rather than win threat in a contested prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and third again two starts back, but winless in its last five starts overall, with a pulled-up effort further back. Already run over today's trip and going and fresh after 20 days, so there's enough consistency for a place without obviously being good enough to win.

runners_data.name: Queensbury Boy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced seven-year-old for Mickey Bowen who won over 25f on good ground (1/25f/GOO) — that form is relevant here; however, with so many prominent types ahead of him in the queue, he is pushed into a midfield role he doesn't naturally fill, and his 26-128 recent form shows sharp enough ability to make the most of any gap that opens.
runners_data.comment: An eighth last time out is the concern, but that followed a runner-up finish two starts back and a win three starts back, so the ability is there. Already run over today's trip and going and fresh after 20 days, a bounce-back would put it into midfield contention.

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the field with an unblemished good-ground profile (15/15 runs), and Patrick O'Brien claims 5lb; the 037-36 recent string includes two thirds, and if the pace quickens mid-race he is the most naturally suited closer, though a slow pace will leave him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, though two thirds among the past five runs show durable form, still without a win in that spell. Already run over today's going before, but a 54-day absence is the obvious query fitness-wise.

runners_data.name: Kingston Narcissus
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combination are in sharp form (T14: 7/26), and this seven-year-old's recent 70-122 sequence shows he is hitting his peak; a natural prominent racer, he presses into a congested midfield because he simply cannot get his position in this field — that limits his chance unless there's early scrimmaging.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and again two starts back, with a win three starts back too — solid recent form. Already run over today's trip and going, fresh after 20 days, and with the yard among the winners lately (7 from its last 26 runners), conditions look to suit.

runners_data.name: In The Air
runners_data.note: Alastair Ralph's eight-year-old has five wins on good ground (5W in 11 good-going runs) and last won over 21f, so the trip and conditions suit; a genuine front-to-prominent horse by inclination, he is squeezed back into midfield by the over-supply — his chance depends on getting closer than his mapped position suggests.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has two wins in its last five starts, and already has experience over today's trip and going. Even so, it sits only 11th of 13 in this field on our figures, meaning it has plenty to find to be competitive.

runners_data.name: St Faz
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Adrian Keatley with a form string of 65746-, the dash denoting a blank last run; stepped up from 16f, and that is the key question for this Adrian Keatley runner — good-ground form exists (2/16f/GOO, 1/16f/GOO) but all wins have come at shorter trips; naturally prominent, he is mapped back involuntarily.
runners_data.comment: Nothing better than a fourth in its last five starts, and yet to score in that spell, leaves this as a stiff task on form. It has run over today's going before and returns 21 days on from its last outing, but sits bottom of our figures in this field.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's nine-year-old has solid form over marathon trips (2/28f/GOO, 3/29f/GOO, 1/25f/SOF) and wears a back bar; his 612-35 recent form reads well at a glance but Ben Godfrey's yard has only 0/2 in the 14-day window; a true stayer who wants further than most of his rivals, his best chance comes in a genuinely run race.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, though that follows a third and a runner-up in the two starts before, plus a win four starts back — genuine ability shown fairly recently. Already run over today's trip and going, but a 41-day layoff and only tenth of 13 on our figures temper the claims.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's seven-year-old carries only 145lbs and has four wins on good ground in his history (4W on good); form reads 146-P2 — the P is a concern — but Shane Fenelon claims 5lb and the horse is a natural hold-up type; a clean jumping round in a run race could see him creep into contention.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out is the headline, though that followed a pulled-up run two starts back and it took until five starts back for the win in this sequence. Already run over today's trip and going, though 12th of 13 on our figures makes this more a placed hope than a winning one.

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Ben Case's seven-year-old has an impressive good-ground record (3W5P from 12 good-ground runs) and arrives on just 19 days' rest in career-best form (14-312); a natural prominent horse pushed into midfield by the field's P-type congestion — if he can work forward from early on he will be a danger, but racing out of role is a meaningful handicap at OR 119.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out with two wins among its last five starts, a scoreline that reads better than its lowly spot on our figures suggests. Already run over today's trip and going and fresh after just 19 days, so fitness won't be the concern here, even if the placing is against it.

races.paceDynamic: Mahons Glory is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no obvious rival to force a serious gallop-battle, Lee Edwards can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable pace over this 2m5½f trip on good ground. The field is deceptively packed with prominent-racing types — Queensbury Boy, Kingston Narcissus, In The Air, St Faz, Stans The Man and Nickelforce are all natural P-style horses who cannot all occupy their preferred early positions, meaning several will be shuffled into an unfamiliar midfield berth and forced to race out of role. Soul Icon, Gunsight Ridge and Breizh River are the genuine P-types most likely to sit behind Mahons Glory in the first rank, while the redistributed runners become involuntary hold-up horses. The resulting race shape — a single, unhurried pace-setter with a contested second tier and a congested, frustrated midfield — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently without having to lead, and who have the tactical fluency to pick off a front-runner going a genuine but not brutal gallop; hold-up horses depending on a fast-run race to finish off will find the slow-burn tempo leaves them with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mahons Glory Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Mahons Glory bowls along at a controlled clip and none of the prominent types are able or willing to push him into a genuinely testing pace.
scenarios.body: Mahons Glory sets a comfortable rhythm that suits his class and recent course form (winner over C&D equivalent distance), and the fractured midfield of redistributed prominent types never organises a sustained challenge; he idles in front and holds on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If one of the genuine second-ranked prominent types — Breizh River or Soul Icon — tracks the leader with cover and produces a clean jump at the last to collar Mahons Glory.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to soften Mahons Glory slightly without breaking him, and a horse like Breizh River (2W7P on similar going, in form: 51-321) or Soul Icon (P-style, Harry Cobden) sweeps past on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo lifts in the middle stages — perhaps Soul Icon or Gunsight Ridge pressing — and the pace-setter ties up, allowing a back-to-form hold-up runner to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Baltic Bird (genuine H-style, 15/15 on good going) or King Roly (4W on good, strong late form) would be the chief beneficiaries, catching a tiring leader close home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent over-supply causes early scrimmaging, positions are scrambled from the outset and one of the nominally midfield-mapped horses gets a cheap lead or ideal pitch.
scenarios.body: Kingston Narcissus (Dan/Harry Skelton, 1W2P recent, sharp form: 70-122) or Queensbury Boy might grab an unexpected prominent berth if the opening stages are fractious, but their out-of-role mapping makes this the least reliable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Breizh River is arriving in strong form (51-321, 2W7P on good) on just 20 days' rest — watch whether Harry Reed sends him into the prime slot directly behind Mahons Glory from the outset, as that position is the race-defining move.

The six redistributed prominent types (Queensbury Boy, Kingston Narcissus, In The Air, St Faz, Stans The Man, Nickelforce) will be jostling for position in the first half-mile — watch for crowding or interference at the early fences that could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Soul Icon's 99-day absence for Keiran Burke is significant — watch his early jumping to see if he is fully tuned up; a mistake at the first or second fence from a horse in Harry Cobden's hands would confirm his layoff is telling.

Baltic Bird is the only genuine hold-up horse with a perfect good-ground profile (15/15) — watch the pace in the final circuit; if Mahons Glory quickens between the last two fences Baltic Bird will be finishing but from too far back, while only a genuine strong gallop gives him a winning chance.

King Roly and Baltic Bird both carry 5lb claimer rides (Fenelon/O'Brien) — watch whether those apprentices are organised enough to get their hold-up horses in a good rhythm early, as a poor position in the back half of the field could cost them their one realistic chance of getting involved.

races.name: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and able to dictate entirely unchallenged; Stuart Edmunds horses carry a 0/1 record in the trainer's 14-day window but she arrives fresh on 29 days' rest with a solid OR=107, wearing headgear, and her Good-ground record includes two wins — her main risk is whether she can maintain the lead long enough once the hold-up horses commit on the turn for home.
runners_data.comment: Hello Sweety arrives as a leading threat, having won three of her last five starts and finishing runner-up last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and the form reads strong, though she's only third of five on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Sun Art
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien in good form (1/9 over 14 days) and this seven-year-old has a consistent recent record with four top-five finishes on Good ground, though his trips have mainly been 2m4f-2m5f and stepping back to 2m½f requires him to show sharper finishing speed than he has recently demonstrated.
runners_data.comment: Sun Art is yet to win in his last five starts but was runner-up two back and third three back, form that puts him top of this field on our figures. He has run over today's trip and going before, returning after a 51-day break.

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's mare arrives after just 22 days' rest and has won twice and placed three times in similar Going conditions in the last 15 comparable runs; she is a natural hold-up performer who will be content to sit at the back and produce a late run, and her form figure of 1 and 2 over 17f at similar trips makes this course and distance combination look well-suited.
runners_data.comment: Jolie Coeur Allen won four starts back and was third two starts back, boosting her claims despite a fourth last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 22-day break, second of five on our figures.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for James Owen, whose trainer's 14-day strike rate of 8/48 is notably strong; this seven-year-old has won three of his last 15 Good-ground runs and his most recent win came over 16f on Good — a genuine hold-up horse whose best form comes when there is a proper pace to aim at.
runners_data.comment: No More Bolero won last time out and three starts back, either side of a third, with two wins from his last four starts. He has run over today's trip and going before, fresh on a 31-day break, but rated only fourth of five on our figures.

runners_data.name: Forest Spirit
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen rides for his father Mickey in what is a competitive booking, but this five-year-old is a true hold-up horse by nature — his form is better over longer trips (20f+) and stepping back to 2m½f means he needs strong fractions to close; mapped into midfield due to the redistribution constraint rather than any natural inclination to race there, his OR=81 makes life harder against these rivals.
runners_data.comment: Forest Spirit is winless in her last five starts, seventh last time out, though she was runner-up two starts back. She has run over today's trip and going before but sits bottom of this field on our figures, making her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Hello Sweety is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no rival willing to take her on from the front, she should be able to dictate an uncontested, controllable gallop over this 2m½f Market Rasen trip on Good ground. Sun Art is the only other prominent-style runner but has been racing over 2m4f-2m5f recently and is unlikely to commit to forcing the pace, meaning Hello Sweety sets the tempo entirely on her own terms. The two genuine hold-up horses, Jolie Coeur Allen and No More Bolero, will be organised off the pace and need either the gallop to quicken late or a strong enough fractions to expose rivals' stamina — with Forest Spirit a true hold-up type shuffled into midfield due to the redistribution constraint. This race shape most favours organised hold-up performers who relish Good ground and can produce a sustained late run, particularly if Hello Sweety's solo lead is comfortable enough to ensure all rivals are travelling within themselves until turning for home, at which point class and finishing kick separate the closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety dictates an honest but not punishing gallop and the hold-up horses have enough left to finish strongly over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Hello Sweety rolls along unchallenged, setting a pace that is sustainable but not slow enough to turn it into a sprint, bringing the field to the last with a compressed group behind; No More Bolero and Jolie Coeur Allen, both effective on Good ground, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces off the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety steals enough of a break through a slow early pace that the hold-up horses cannot close the gap fully on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages gives Hello Sweety a soft lead and she pings the hurdles fluently, arriving at the final flight full of running with nothing able to bridge the gap quickly enough on this sharp track; Sun Art, travelling prominently throughout, is best placed of the chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Art pushes up to press Hello Sweety and the early gallop is more genuine, stretching the field and turning it into a stamina battle.
scenarios.body: Fractions quicken enough that Hello Sweety is tested sooner than she would like, bringing staying power to the fore over the final half-mile; No More Bolero, who has three wins on Good ground at 2m and loves this trip, has the profile to grind out a win from off the pace in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Midfield Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is entirely false and the race collapses into a tactical crawl followed by a flat-out dash from three out.
scenarios.body: Forest Spirit, a genuine hold-up type pushed forward into midfield in the mapping, struggles to get into the race at all, reducing the scenario's plausibility; Sun Art, with good positional speed and a recent Good-ground placing, is better placed than most to cope with a sprint finish from a handy berth.

watchPoints.text: Hello Sweety leads unchallenged from the front — if she builds even a two-length cushion into the back straight with no pursuer applying pressure, her ability to control tempo could be decisive for held-up rivals.
No More Bolero's jockey Harry Cobden is significant — Cobden typically delivers hold-up horses precisely and a good jump at the last could be the winning move if the pace has softened rivals ahead.

Sun Art's optimal distance is 2m4f-2m5f and this 2m½f trip is shorter than ideal; watch whether Jack Hogan commits him prominently early to compensate, which could alter the pace dynamic significantly.

Forest Spirit's true hold-up style is compromised by the race shape — if he is unable to find his natural position at the rear, Sean Bowen may have to make decisions mid-race that are uncharacteristic for this horse.

With only five runners on Good ground at Market Rasen, the tempo could become very dawdly in the back straight — watch the first three hurdles to gauge whether Hello Sweety is allowed to build any margin or is effectively jogging in company.

races.name: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Consistent good-ground performer (12/15 strike-rate in similar conditions) with a recent course win; natural hold-up horse who will need either a strong pace or a patient ride from Charlie Todd to get competitive, and at 2m1f — the shorter end of his recent trips — there may not be enough time to reel in a front-runner if the fractions are modest.
runners_data.comment: Catchim was only fourth last time out but the formline includes a win four starts back and a second two starts back, showing more than the bare result suggests. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 19-day break, with that recent placed form the case for taking him on here.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's charge returns after 42 days off and has two wins from hold-up tactics on good ground; the longer break is a mild concern given T14 of 2/13 suggests the yard is not in peak form, and at OR 99 he is the highest-rated runner but needs the pace to collapse in front of him — unlikely with only one genuine front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Dream Jet is winless in his last five starts and was only eighth last time out, though he has been placed twice in that spell, third both two and four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, is fresh on a 42-day break, and tops our figures here despite the lack of a win.

runners_data.name: Sledgehammer
runners_data.note: Oakley Brown takes the 5lb claim on this lightly-built six-year-old whose recent form reads 5P6-64 — uninspiring — and who has failed to place in any of his last five good-ground starts; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, he is mapped to midfield because the field is congested at the rear, meaning he will likely race further forward than he wants, blunting his chances.
runners_data.comment: Sledgehammer is winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up effort four starts back, and nothing better than fourth across that run. He has run over today's going before and returns quickly on a 15-day break, but the modest form leaves him only sixth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on good ground 11 days ago (form: 4P9-13, recent win notable) and races off OR 90 with headgear (hood/p); David Bridgwater's runner is a true hold-up type shuffled into the midfield map due to rear-end congestion, and though his recent course-trip-going win is the standout form line, his ability to reproduce it from a non-natural position is the question.
runners_data.comment: Most Wanted won two starts back having gone through a rough patch that included a ninth and a pulled-up run, and was third last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and is quick to load on an 11-day turnaround, rated third of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Prospect House
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's eight-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in this field and goes in blinkers (v) — headgear that often sharpens jumping focus — ridden by a 3lb claimer; his task is simply to bowl along at a comfortable clip, jump cleanly, and ensure he has enough left from the two-out fence, which at this distance on good ground at Market Rasen is very achievable.
runners_data.comment: Prospect House was third last time out, continuing a solid run of form that includes a win three starts back and a second five back. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 36-day break, with the consistent placed form making him a leading danger at fourth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's veteran (9yo, T14: 0/17) returns after just 11 days and has posted two wins and good placed efforts at around 2m on soft, though his good-ground figures are a notch below (7/15 sim-going strike-rate); wears a visor and races prominently, giving him the best position to track Prospect House and challenge — his recency and prominent style make him the most natural second lead.
runners_data.comment: Huit Reflets is winless in his last five starts but was placed second in two of his last five, four and five starts back, with more moderate efforts since including a ninth two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on an 11-day turnaround, sitting fifth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Mr McWhinny
runners_data.note: T Ellis's runner won last time out (form: F57-14) and races with a tongue-tie; good ground suits him well (13/15 sim-going), but his longer trips in history (up to 26f) suggest 2m1f might be sharp, and as a true hold-up horse placed into a midfield role by race circumstances, he will need fortune in running and clean jumping to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Mr McWhinny was fourth last time out and did win two starts back, but a fall and a seventh among his other starts temper the appeal. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 35-day break, though seventh of eight on our figures says he has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's runner recorded three pulled-up efforts before signs of life with a 5th and 7th; raced just six days ago and the quick turnaround is a flag, especially for a horse wearing a tongue-tie and whose form string reads PP-P57; a genuine hold-up type repositioned toward midfield by default, and with OR 69 the lowest-rated runner, his chances depend more on others failing than on his own strengths.
runners_data.comment: Fox Wallace is winless in her last five starts and has failed to complete on three of them, seventh last time out having also been pulled up in three of her previous four. She has run over today's trip and going before and is race-fit on a rapid 6-day turnaround, but sits bottom of eight on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Prospect House is the lone confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner handicap chase over 2m1f on good ground at Market Rasen, and with no genuine rival willing or able to press him hard, he is set to control the gallop from the front and dictate a measured, sustainable tempo throughout. The remainder of the field — Catchim, Dream Jet, Sledgehammer, Most Wanted, Mr McWhinny, and Fox Wallace — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, with Huit Reflets offering the only other prominent profile to at least give Prospect House some loose company. This field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Sledgehammer, Most Wanted, Mr McWhinny, and Fox Wallace are all genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed to midfield, meaning several will race in unfamiliar positions and not all can execute their preferred style. A single, uncontested front-runner dictating a fair pace on good ground at a track that does not brutally punish leaders — Market Rasen being a relatively flat, galloping right-hand circuit — creates conditions that strongly favour the prominent racer who can conserve energy in front, jump fluently, and find a gear at the last; horses with a patient, hold-up style are disadvantaged because the pace is unlikely to be hot enough to set them up for a late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prospect House Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Prospect House bowls along unchallenged, controls the fractions, and jumps fluently throughout.
scenarios.body: Prospect House, ridden by claimer William Maggs (3lb claim), sets his own pace with no rival willing to press him, arriving at the final fence full of running and kicking clear; Huit Reflets, also prominent, is best placed of the chasers to pick up any scraps if Prospect House flattens out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the prominent runners tire on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Catchim and Dream Jet — the two highest-rated hold-up horses with solid good-ground form records — make significant headway from the home turn and overhaul a weakening Prospect House; this scenario depends on the tempo being hotter than expected, which is unlikely without a genuine pace rival.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses race unexpectedly prominently, bunching occurs early and the race develops into a rough-and-tumble contest with a muddled tempo.
scenarios.body: With Sledgehammer, Most Wanted, Mr McWhinny, and Fox Wallace all unable to slot into their natural rear positions, the early order becomes congested and mistakes or interference unsettles the race shape; Most Wanted, who has shown he can win at this trip on good ground and was recording a recent victory, could capitalise if he adapts best to a forward position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fluent Jumper Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If a horse in midfield produces a round of outstanding jumping to make up ground through the air and arrives late with momentum.
scenarios.body: A clean-jumping midfield racer picks off tiring rivals with slick leaps at the later fences; Mr McWhinny, wearing a tongue-tie and suited by good ground based on his course-and-distance profile, is the likeliest beneficiary of this niche shape despite racing out of his natural hold-up role.

watchPoints.text: Prospect House — if he slots into a clean lead jumping the first and clears the second fence without any rival crowding him, the race shape is set and he becomes very difficult to peg back at this 2m1f trip.

Most Wanted — his win 11 days ago over course and trip is the most relevant recent form line in the race, but watch whether Brendan Powell attempts to ride him more forward than usual given the rear congestion; if he gets a clear run, he is the most dangerous hold-up type.

Huit Reflets — monitor his jumping in the early stages; if he travels smoothly in second behind Prospect House and meets his fences well, he becomes the main on-course threat without needing the pace to collapse.

Sledgehammer and Fox Wallace — both natural hold-up horses forced into unnatural positions; watch the early-race bunching around the third to fifth fences where interference or a mistake from either could disrupt the midfield and open the race up for others.

Dream Jet (42-day break) — Patrick Wadge will need to get him settled quickly if he comes out fresh after the layoff; any early keenness from a natural hold-up type would be counter-productive in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring him into it late anyway.

races.name: Betway Boosts Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Special John
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with winning form at 24f on Good in his last start; carries top weight of 170lbs and races off OR 112, but his ability to dictate from the front on Good ground at Market Rasen is his defining asset, though the 3m trip may test his stamina at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and with a win two starts back plus another second three starts back, the form has been solid across its last five starts. Already run over today's trip and going, though a pair of fifths further back and 38 days off are worth noting before backing it up in class.

runners_data.name: Yes Day
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who wants a searching gallop to deliver his best, and his sim-going record of 11 runs at 2W5P on similar conditions is solid; headgear (blinkers) may sharpen his focus but he is reliant on a pace scenario that this race may only partially provide.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out having been a close second the run before, with a quick fitness turnaround after just 17 days. Already run over today's trip and going and tops this field on our figures, though it remains without a win in its last five starts.

runners_data.name: Giovanni Change
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old prominent racer who has placed in ten of his last fifteen runs on similar going, including a win over 24f on Good; Mark Walford's yard is 0/17 in the last 14 days which is worth noting, but the horse's consistency at this style and ground profile makes him hard to overlook.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, but that follows back-to-back thirds and a win four starts back, so the underlying form is stronger than the final placing suggests. Already run over today's trip and going, though 42 days off and a pulled-up effort further back are the queries against it.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: In-form 6-year-old who has won his last two starts and arrives with momentum; Shane Fenelon claims 5lb which softens the burden at 161lbs, and his prominent racing style suits a race run at measured tempo, though blinkers on suggests he needs keeping up to his work.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and again two starts back, backed up by a third three starts back and a runner-up four starts back — plenty of recent placed form on the board. Already run over today's trip and going, but 42 days off and only fifth of seven on our figures leave it needing to bounce straight back to form.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rambler
runners_data.note: Sound record on Good ground with 12 of 15 sim-going runs in the frame, but his natural prominent style cannot be reproduced here as he is pushed into a midfield berth by the weight of front-running competition — visor headgear may help, though Freddie Keighley also claims 5lb.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, though that came after a win two starts back and a further third five starts back, so there's solid ability in the mix. Already run over today's trip and going, but a 42-day absence and a modest recent finish leave a slight question over sharpness.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Lightly framed hold-up performer whose best form has come on Soft; his sim-going record on Good is thin at 5 runs with one win, and a last run of just 13 days ago off a poor effort (form string ending in 0) raises freshness questions despite the tongue tie.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, and pulled up two starts back, a poor recent sequence despite a win and a runner-up further back. Already run over today's trip and going and freshened up after just 13 days, but sits bottom of our figures in this field of seven.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with only three runs on Good ground and a best performance of 3rd at 17f, so the 3m trip and Good surface both present uncertainty; Charlie Maggs claims 3lb and the horse arrives fresh at 20 days, but limited evidence at this distance makes it hard to be confident.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and third again three starts back, either side of a below-par seventh, with a runner-up four starts back. Yet to win in that spell, though already run over today's trip and going and fresh after 20 days — sixth of seven on our figures is a stiff ask.

races.paceDynamic: Special John is the confirmed front runner and, with only one horse genuinely likely to lead, will control the tempo unchallenged over the 3m trip on Good ground at Market Rasen, setting a measured, sustainable gallop that rewards those who can travel comfortably in his slipstream. Giovanni Change and Sir Carnegie are genuine prominent types who will press for the positions immediately behind Special John, creating a fairly ordered early order with limited scrapping for pace. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than the shape can accommodate — Redbridge Rambler is a true prominent racer who will be squeezed back further than ideal, and Millena Agent, a natural hold-up performer, has been mapped to midfield where the true rear contingent is compressed. With one uncontested leader setting an honest but not brutal tempo over three miles, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel in a rhythm and pick off the leader approaching the final fences — genuine hold-up horses who need a stronger pace to be set may find the race not run to suit their needs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Special John Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Special John leads unchallenged at a fair gallop and the prominent chasers cannot reel him in off the final turn.
scenarios.body: Special John dictates from the front with no rival applying sustained pressure, conserving energy for a strong finish over the last three fences; prominent horses Giovanni Change and Sir Carnegie who travel close to him are best placed to pounce if he does weaken, but horses with course form on Good ground thrive here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Special John sets a pace that gives way approaching the last mile and one of the tracking prominent horses swoops past.
scenarios.body: Giovanni Change, an 11-year-old with consistent placed form at 24f on Good ground, or Sir Carnegie, who arrives in fine nick with back-to-back wins, track the leader into the straight and find extra when Special John is caught out by the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up horse picks up the pieces in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Yes Day, a genuine hold-up performer with two wins and five places to his name on similar going, is the most credible beneficiary if the race is run at a tempo that burns off the leaders by the final fence; You Did is younger but inconsistent on Good ground and carries a recent poor run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Disruption, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If key prominent horses jump poorly or fall, fragmenting the pace scenario and opening the race up to the fringe contenders.
scenarios.body: Redbridge Rambler, unable to secure his natural prominent berth, could benefit if he forces his way forward and the other prominent horses empty simultaneously; Millena Agent is less convincing here given limited form at the trip and only three runs on Good ground.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Redbridge Rambler is allowed to stride forward at the start — if Freddie Keighley pushes him to secure a prominent position rather than accepting midfield, it reshapes the whole pace picture and may force Special John into a contested lead.

Yes Day's chance is sensitive to tempo — if Special John dawdles in front and the field bunches, McLernon will have little room to deliver a hold-up run and the scenario that suits him most simply won't materialise.

Sir Carnegie's back-to-back winning form is compelling but the step up to 3m is a new test for the 6-year-old; watch his jumping in the latter stages as tire over fences at this trip is a genuine risk for a horse who hasn't been asked this question before.

You Did ran just 13 days ago and posted a poor effort (form figure 0); if that run was interrupted by a problem, Brian Ellison's runners returning quickly can occasionally bounce back, but monitor any market moves as an indicator of stable confidence.

races.name: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist who has been placed at this trip on good ground recently, but Tom Midgley's 3lb claim is a useful nudge and trainer Sam England is running at 1/6 over 14 days — workload context worth noting; needs the race to fall apart late to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out but that followed a win two starts back and a runner-up four starts back, form that marks it out as the pick of this field on our figures. Already run over today's trip and going and fit again after 27 days, with only a flat seventh three starts back as the blemish.

runners_data.name: Prince Quattro
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on this 7yo who won on good ground but has only one hit from five attempts on similar going since; hold-up style means he is dependent on a strong pace and a clear run, and his recent outings at Stanton/Stafford-style tracks may not fully translate here.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, backed by two wins three and four starts back, so there's plenty of ability on view across the last five starts. Already run over today's going before and fresh after 22 days, though seventh of 12 on our figures suggests there's a touch more needed to feature at the top.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has been consistent in placed efforts at this trip on good ground, making the first three in his last two starts; Oakley Brown's 5lb claim helps the weight but as a genuine hold-up runner he needs the race to develop in his favour — no pace concerns on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and third again two starts back, a pair of placed efforts that put it among the leading dangers here. Yet to win in that spell though, with an unplaced run and modest finishes further back, and already run over today's trip and going, so it needs the placed form to translate into more.

runners_data.name: Arnie Moon
runners_data.note: Young 6yo who won at 16f on good and has placed at this trip before; Callum Pritchard rides and trainer Joe Tickle has sent three from ten recently — the horse shapes as a hold-up type whose best form comes around or under today's distance.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, having fallen the run before that, though a win three starts back and a third five starts back show there's ability when things go right. Already run over today's going before and fresh after 31 days, but the interruption from that fall is a fitness question mark.

runners_data.name: Vivid Pink
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and has won twice at 2m4f on good ground; Tom Bellamy partners a horse that has shown she can dictate and sustain, and the absence of any rival willing to press her early makes her tactical position uniquely powerful here.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and again two starts back, a pair of victories that stand out in a shorter recent sequence of just four starts. Already run over today's trip and going and fresh after 29 days, but tenth of 12 on our figures leaves plenty to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Ballygeary
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature though shown in midfield on the map given the crowded rear; Mike Sowersby sends him out on a quick turnaround (20 days) and he has zero wins from 15 good-ground starts — the lack of a victory in these conditions is a significant flag regardless of positioning.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and third again four starts back, with a 5th, 6th and 7th filling in the rest of its last five starts. Still without a win in that spell, though it ranks second-highest in this field on our figures — the placed form just needs to convert.

runners_data.name: Twist Of Fatecatch
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a standout jockey booking for a prominent-style runner who has placed at 2m3f and 2m4f on good going; best suited to tracking the pace and pouncing, which is exactly the position available just behind Vivid Pink — the most natural tactical fit in this field beyond the leader.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, though a third two starts back and two fourths either side of an unplaced effort show there's been solid consistency in this spell, just without a win to show for it. Already run over today's trip and going, but 35 days off is the query before it can be fully trusted.

runners_data.name: Shesonnet
runners_data.note: In reality a hold-up operator who gets nudged into a midfield slot here; ran just two days ago which is an extremely quick turnaround and Ben Case has had no winners from three in the past 14 days — freshness and trainer form are both concerns even if the mare has placed form on good ground.

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: Likes good ground and has filled the runner-up berth on it twice recently at 2m3f and 2m4f; Jonathan Burke takes the ride for James Owen (trainer also runs Prince Quattro), and while this horse's hold-up instincts are pushed into midfield on the map, his proven ability to finish well at this trip makes him one of the more credible threats.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and again two starts back, backed by two thirds back-to-back after that — a genuinely consistent recent record, even without a win to show for it. Already run over today's trip and going and freshest in the field having run just 8 days ago, which sixth of 12 on our figures fairly reflects.

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back course wins on good ground and wears tongue-tie; a natural hold-up horse shunted into midfield by the congested rear, but his Market Rasen course form is a legitimate positive — the 48 days since last run is a slight unknown, though his first run back last time produced a win.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and again two starts back, with a third also in that spell — strong recent scoring form on the board. Already run over today's trip and going, but 48 days off is a lengthy gap and eighth of 12 on our figures tempers how far it can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Saxon Cross
runners_data.note: No wins from seven good-ground starts and has finished 5th or worse in all five of his last outings; a hold-up type mapped to midfield because of field congestion, but the flat recent form and inability to win on this surface make him hard to fancy regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and yet to finish in the frame across its last five starts, a poor recent sequence that's hard to overlook. Already run over today's going before and fit enough after 44 days, but ninth of 12 on our figures is a fair reflection of the form on show.

runners_data.name: Modern Style
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted 4yo who has won twice on good going and showed solid form in three from four placed efforts; James Davies rides for Nigel Hawke (0/1 in 14 days) and his hold-up style is pushed midfield — his youth and upward trajectory are the main arguments for him, though he steps up in company here.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, following a runner-up and two wins in the three starts before that — a strong sequence that makes its lowly spot on our figures a surprise. Already run over today's going before, though 45 days off is a long enough gap to raise a fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Mojo Ego
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 16f on good but that was a shorter trip than today's 2m4½f; Fergal O'Brien (1/9 in 14 days) sends him out 17 days after that win, and this is a hold-up horse thrust into a midfield slot — the step up in trip and handicap company is unproven territory.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, a clear step forward after a run of finishes no better than fourth in the four starts before it. Already run over today's going before and fresh again after just 17 days, but bottom of our figures in this field means it has plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Vivid Pink is the confirmed and sole front-runner in this 13-runner field, and with no credible rival to push her early, she can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good ground over 2m4½f — a trip and surface where she has won twice already. The chasing pack is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, meaning the race will almost certainly develop into a single-file procession behind Vivid Pink for much of the journey, with challengers forced to cover ground from well off the pace. Several runners carrying [REDISTRIBUTED] tags — including Ballygeary, Shesonnet, Oneinthewell, Nottodaybobo, Saxon Cross, Modern Style and Mojo Ego — are genuine hold-up horses who cannot all travel at the back in a 13-runner field; the most likely to negotiate midfield positions and secure a decent berth are Oneinthewell and Shesonnet, who have the tactical profiles and recent form to adapt. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: this shape strongly favours either the front-runner if the pace is gentle enough to preserve energy, or the very few genuine prominent/mid-pack horses who can travel into contention without burning fuel — true deep closers will face a stern test if Vivid Pink sets a sustainable rhythm and the race lacks the scorching pace needed to bring them into play late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vivid Pink Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Vivid Pink bowls along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the hold-up brigade cannot generate the finishing burst to peg her back.
scenarios.body: Tom Bellamy settles Vivid Pink in front and, facing zero early pressure on good ground, she conserves enough energy to extend her winning run at this trip; her two recent wins at 2m4f on good confirm she handles conditions perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Mid-Pack
scenarios.trigger: If Vivid Pink's tempo is slightly quicker than ideal and one of the genuinely good hold-up horses picks up strongly from two out.
scenarios.body: Oneinthewell or Shesonnet, who are capable of tracking mid-division after their redistributed placement, get into a rhythm and launch sustained late challenges; both have the recent placed form on good ground to suggest they can finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Fades, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally too ambitious and Twist Of Fatecatch, travelling prominently just off Vivid Pink, pounces when the leader weakens approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Harry Cobden positions Twist Of Fatecatch handily in second or third throughout, and a flat-spots moment from Vivid Pink hands the initiative to this confirmed prominent type; his placed record at this trip on good ground underpins the claim.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning for home and creates a genuine sprint finish that rewards the deepest-sitting, freshest legs in the field.
scenarios.body: Glory And Honour or Prince Quattro, racing off a patient hold-up ride, find clear daylight late and close with a sustained run down the straight; this scenario is less likely given so many true closers are occupying midfield positions rather than their natural rear-of-field berth, diluting the finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Vivid Pink's early position is the key lever in this race — if Tom Bellamy finds she can stride into an uncontested lead at the first fence, the tempo she sets will shape every other runner's fate; watch for any horse pressing her before the back straight.
Shesonnet's two-day turnaround is unusually quick and could blunt her finishing effort; watch for signs of tiredness from three out if she has not fully recovered from her last outing.

Oneinthewell's jockey Jonathan Burke also trains stable-companion Prince Quattro for the same yard — with two runners, watch how Burke positions Oneinthewell early, as his ride may be shaped around not interfering with the yard's other representative.

Nottodaybobo has won twice at Market Rasen on good ground, which is a meaningful course advantage in an otherwise flat recent record for several rivals; watch whether Joshua Thompson can get him into a handy position from midfield given his hold-up instincts.

The weight of hold-up horses forced into midfield roles creates a risk of bunching and interference at the second-last hurdle when they all commit simultaneously — watch for crowding as the field compresses on the final bend.
